title: ReSI: Recursive Safety Improvement toward Resistant and Resilient AI
abstract: arXiv:2610.12233v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recursive self-improvement, the participation of AI systems in improving their own capabilities, is beginning to move from theoretical prospect to practice, posing both challenges and opportunities for safety alignment. Models evolve through frequent updates, and their safety alignment requires continual adaptation to each new checkpoint. Meanwhile, with evolving red-teaming methods exposing new vulnerabilities, safety improvement for each checkpoint needs to mitigate exposed vulnerabilities and generalize to risks not yet revealed. Following R$^2$AI, we term these goals resistance to known threats and resilience to unforeseen risks. Recursive self-improvement, in turn, inspires an approach to both goals: safety alignment could likewise advance through successive rounds of evaluation and update. translated_title: ReSI：面向抗性与韧性的递归安全改进
translated_abstract: 递归自我改进——即AI系统参与提升自身能力的过程——正开始从理论前景走向实践，这为安全对齐既带来了挑战也带来了机遇。模型通过频繁的更新而不断演化，其安全对齐需要针对每个新的检查点进行持续适配。与此同时，随着红队测试方法不断演进并暴露出新的漏洞，针对每个检查点的安全改进既需要缓解已暴露的漏洞，也需要泛化到尚未显现的风险上。继R²AI之后，我们将这些目标称为对已知威胁的“抗性”以及对未知风险的“韧性”。反过来，递归自我改进也启发了一种实现这两个目标的方法：安全对齐同样可以通过一轮又一轮的评估与更新来不断推进。为此，我们提出了ReSI，一个通过自动化研究来实现这一方法的递归安全改进框架。在每一轮中，
tldr: 提出ReSI递归安全改进框架，通过自动化研究驱动的多轮评估与更新循环，使AI安全对齐同时具备抵御已知威胁的“抗性”和应对未知风险的“韧性”。
en_tdlr: ReSI is a recursive safety improvement framework that leverages automated research in iterative rounds of evaluation and update, making AI safety alignment both resistant to known threats and resilient to unforeseen risks.
